title: Rollout signal contract and hypothesis harvest for staged-model regression
creator: Sofia Chen
description: After the 2025-02-07 staged rollout that triggered an automated rollback, we need a concise, machine-readable 'rollback signal contract' and an exhaustive hypothesis log. The goal is to (1) define deterministic signals that should trigger an automated rollback or alert, (2) capture the set of plausible root-cause hypotheses observed during the incident, and (3) update the runbook, CI checks, and dashboards so future rollouts surface the same signals earlier with less manual triage.
summary: Create a single source-of-truth for rollout signal thresholds, telemetry to collect for canaries/shadows/A-Bs, and a prioritized remediation backlog derived from the hypothesis harvest.
decision_log: 2025-02-10: Triage call decided to treat this as a safety contract task rather than individual incident fixes; owner assigned to ENG-82019.
2025-02-11: Agreed to include model-quality signals (eval regression on canary prompt set) in the rollback contract in addition to infra signals.

2025-02-13: Decided to require 'signal amplification' rule: only trigger auto-rollback when at least two distinct signal classes breach thresholds within a rolling 3-minute window unless severity is P0-critical.
2025-02-14: PM requested customer-facing post explaining why a rollback happened; include templated language in the runbook.
steps_taken: Collected raw telemetry from canary window: p50/p95/p99 latency, 5xx rate, model eval drift score, embedding cosine-distribution shift, prefix cache miss rate, memory pressure traces.
Ran offline replay of the canary traffic against previous model revision to isolate regressions that are model-only vs infra-related.
Instrumented additional synthetic prompts (30 prompt probes) to exercise hallucination-sensitive behavior and added them to the canary evaluation suite.
Added temporary shadow routing for 15% of production traffic to capture real-world prompts for deeper diagnostics.
Filed a hotfix PR that tightened batching heuristics; ran unit + perf tests but did not merge until the signal contract and runbook were in place.
hypothesis_harvest: Quantization kernel mismatch: new quantized variant produced distributional token score changes causing hallucinations on rare prompts.
KV cache invalidation bug under certain concurrent batching patterns leading to stale context used during generation.
Autoscaler bounce after a transient spike caused higher cold-start latency and request timeouts, amplifying user-visible errors.
Model prompt-change interaction: small change in system prompt applied only in the new rollout produced edge-case cascading behavior on structured-output routes.
Routing fallback to CPU variant under GPU contention increased latency and reduced generation quality for long-context requests.
Telemetry misaggregation: aggregation window mismatch made apparent spike look wider than it was (false positive); contract should prevent single-source reliance.
External dependency (third-party tokenizer library) regression when handling uncommon Unicode sequences.

acceptance_criteria: Rollback contract YAML exists in infra-config repo and is referenced by the rollout orchestrator.
At least three telemetry sources (infra latency, error-rate, model-eval drift) are wired into the composite rollback-risk score in Grafana.
Runbook updated with templated communications and triage matrix; security/privacy checklist completed.
CI gating: canary eval suite runs in PRs for model-serving changes and fails fast on detected regressions.
Hypothesis archive completed and prioritized backlog created with owners and due dates.
Two-signal amplification rule implemented and tested in a staging rollout.
Customer-facing post explaining the rollback is drafted and approved by PM + Legal.
